After playing this game for a good 350+ hours I feel that I can give an accurate enough review on this absolutely massive beast of a game. I'm not an expert writer or reviewer, so bear with me and my poor english skills. Please also keep in mind that I haven't played this game in quite a while, but from the look of things the experience seems to be mostly the same as it was when I did.

---

This game is pretty good. There's tons of content to do and systems to get into, but that's where one of its biggest problems lies. There's just [i] too much content. [/i] This game's entire gameplay loop revolves around grinding, grinding, and then more grinding. Guns, frames, materials, levels, everything is based on grinding. You can buy all kinds of skips, boosts and instant-access to most of the items in the game, which is to be expected of a free to play game, and I wouldn't say it's forced on you, but there are [i] many [/i] times where it will give you not-so-subtle nudges towards the cash shop. Most in-game store items are bought with a standard premium currency with the "buy either not enough or just a bit too much" that gives you constant incentive to buy just a bit more so you can afford that cool shiny thing.

With 5 major expansions over the last 9 years, Warframe has received tons of new content quite consistently with overall positive reception. Hardcore veterans of this game are able to experience new content the day it comes out as they have had enough time to prepare for every new expansion and update. As a new player though, you start from the bottom. 9 Years of grinding is a lot to catch up on, and it can be hard to do so when the game keeps throwing new systems and shiny collectables at you. Sure you can just buy the best stuff, but that doesn't boost you much further in the story or make you understand the game more. 

Digital Extremes has a bit of a reputation for being very community focused with their livestreams and constant updates, adding bits of player-created content every now and then to keep people invested and creating new things. However, when you experience your first big update as a player, you soon realise that DE just kind of... doesn't fully know why they implement some systems. Things are broken or buggy on release and take so long to tweak that they just get given up on.


The combat is the main focus of the game. It feels great and intuitive with flashy moves and fast action. Perfect for turning your brain off and listening to music for an hour or two while you mow down hordes of enemies. It's satisfying and repetitive. 90% Of what you will be actively spending your time on is entering missions, killing x number of enemies or collecting/destroying a thing, and then getting out. PvP is playable and enjoying for a little while, but is also highly repetitive and doesn't really reward you with anything.


Endgame doesn't exist. You collect more stuff, customize your Warframe, and wait for the next patch while doing so. Once new content comes out you do it again. It's not bad by any means because that's basically what you're doing the entire time you play this game.

---

TLDR:
Warframe is a fast-paced grindfest where you kill enemies, craft new gear from materials you collect, and check the wiki 5000 times to figure out where said materials can be collected. It's mostly simple, low-effort content that's fun to play either alone or with friends. It's definitely worth a try if mindlessly killing enemies in space sounds like a good time to you. Even if it doesn't you can probably still squeeze some fun out of it. It's free to play so there's nothing to lose but time.
its really fun but you must be a person that likes grinding to play this game
